newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union leader threatens to spurn EMU.
newsitem.headline: German union leader threatens to spurn EMU.

text.p: The German government was warned on Saturday not to gamble away union and other support for the European single currency by implementing further social spending cuts to meet euro entry criteria.

Ursula Engelen-Kefer, vice chairman of the Federation of German trade unions (DGB), said "I warn the government: further cuts in social spending for the euro will be the stumbling block, the breaking point the government won't be able to get past."
"It will gamble away the support of the DGB and the Social Democrats for the euro," she said in an interview with the Cologne daily Express published on Saturday
Finance Minister Theo Waigel is expected to announce on Friday a supplementary budget for 1997 with a deficit eight to 10 billion marks higher than originally planned.
Further spending cuts would hamper economic expansion, coalition sources said.
The new budget will still be in line with the entry requirements for EMU, the sources said.
